//: Routing and caching for the static build in dist/.
Rewrites run after the filesystem check, so /services still resolves
straight to the prerendered dist/services/index.html and never touches
the catch-all below. Only a path matching no real file falls through to
it — a plain static deployment does not serve dist/404.html on its own,
so without this rewrite an unknown URL hit Vercel's own NOT_FOUND page
instead of the site's branded one.
//trailingSlash: Matches the canonical tags, which name /services rather than /services/.
Vercel 308s the slashed form to the bare one, so only one of the two ever

//: The apex to www 301. Kept here rather than only in the dashboard so
the canonical host is recorded in the repo alongside the tags that
depend on it — every canonical, og:url and sitemap entry names www,
and without this redirect both hosts would serve the whole site.
Harmless if the dashboard already redirects: that happens at the edge
first and this never matches.
Catch-all, evaluated only for a path that matched no real file. It
serves dist/404.html's markup — the branded page, the noindex meta
tag, the empty JSON-LD — but a rewrite cannot change the response's
status code, so this answers 200 rather than 404. The noindex tag is
what actually keeps a JS-rendering crawler from indexing it; Google
treats that as equivalent to a 404/410 for de-indexing purposes. A
non-JS crawler reading raw status codes is the one audience this
does not fully satisfy — closing that gap needs a serverless
function or Vercel's legacy `routes` config instead of `rewrites`.
Asset filenames carry a content hash, so a given URL's bytes never
change and the response can be cached indefinitely.
The HTML is not hashed and now carries the prerendered content, so a
cached copy would keep serving yesterday's markup and yesterday's
asset URLs after a deploy. Revalidate every time.
